P&L:

going thru all ur losses and troubleshooting. process vs outcome, luck vs skill, learning from ur mistakes

this sounds very simple, and I sat down to write a tweet-length answer....4000 words later was like, oh shit 

there's actually so many layers to it

but this to me is the most important, its the #1 way to improve, people who are serious do it

and yet no one does it 

because it sucks. it's you alone in a dark room by yourself, just staring at all ur bad decisions

2.

u want to know why 99.9% of people really don't do it?

they don't want to know the truth about themselves. the truth is ugly. they're afraid to look inside, because they don't know what they'll find.

and your P&L leaves you NOWHERE TO HIDE.

it is a mirror, and it's an unvarnished reflection of all your flaws, your bad decisions and your dogshit discipline

u cannot blame or make excuses, u cannot tweet around it, and it is immune to all forms of LARPitude

it's one of the clearest indicators of who is real not just as a trader but as a human

show me someone who is afraid to look at their P&L, and give me moneyline at -1000

lay $10k to win $1000 that they will never be successful in markets

its that simple

3.

if there were prop bets I'd tell u exactly how they blow their first account...time horizon, position sizes 

first off I've made every mistake myself, and second, over 10-15 years of trading, teaching friends/family, watching people fail in years 0-5 over and over and over...

I just know all the early-stage mistakes, especially the mental/cognitive ones, ego, vanity, denial, self-deceit, fear

someone in years 0-5 of trading markets is a fucking mess, like an asylum case...they underestimate how stupid, weak, and slippery the human mind is

4.

tell a guy "stop urself out down 20%" "okay"

takes a 60% loss

"what happened there chief? ur job was to see the number 20%, and then click the mouse....a 6-year old coulda done that"

mfs will either lose their shit, crumble, or enable some sociopath mode where the loss wasn't their fault

all people's fucked up childhoods and upbringings emerge in how they grapple with harsh truths

u see people who are knotted up too tight where u don't think they could ever be unwound

nothing is ever their fault, ever, and never will be

there are lots of people like this on twtr, in 2-3 sentences u can immediately discern how someone handles accountability and responsability

the human brain is frightening

so thats P&L.

1. grinding charts/running screens

I learned this from a boss back in the day, whose process wasn't too far off from this

Stan Druckenmiller: Okay, so every night, at about 4:30, I get 272 charts. They cover just about every group in the stock market, every commodity, every currency cross I'm interested, in every fixed income market around the world. And they're basically daily, weekly, and monthly. Daily supposed to predict 8-20 days, weekly 8-20 weeks, and monthly 8-20 months. When I make an investment decision, it's usually--sometimes, believe it or not: The idea comes from the charts, but I will never invest just on a chart. But if I really like a fundamental thesis and the chart stinks, I won't do it.

Druck trades macro, a L/S manager will have 500-1000 equity charts on top of that, diff time frames than Druck

you can do it post-close or pre-open

Druck and my boss were early AM, I always preferred doing it after the close

20-30 mins as a wind-down, just subconsciously uploading everything that happened during the day

here is a free screener I have always used

https://t.co/l8VF2TbITD

daily post-close, I do:

descriptive tab: "mkt cap > $300m"
technical tab: 52-week highs (1st screen) 52-week lows (2nd screen)

thats two diff screens, 52-week highs, and 52-week lows, both with $300m min (smalls mkt cap)

then, click "Charts" below all the toggles

this shows u where $ is sloshing in and out of, what's working, what isn't

u actually can use it for idea gen, because the market will always move first

before anyone has spilled a drop of ink, price has moved

everything is downstream of price

so when u see an odd move in a name that everyone has forgotten about, a name you knew well at one point, but that no one is talking about...

...and suddenly its printing 52w highs, on volume, on no news?

immediate "invest first and then investigate," in 24-48 hours you can get current

odds are always way better than 51-49 that fundamentals are inflecting, these trades are high hit rate because it's all incremental buyers from here

remember, no ink has been spilled yet

and there hasn't been any news

all u have is johnny-come-lately shorts getting taken out and the oddball deep value buyers, and now u prob have faster money, small L/S SM, prop desks, the minnows are there, the big fish

Druck talks about this but the fast, hard part of the move, is always when there's no news and no logic...u buy off instinct, bc u recognize the pattern, but u know that u are making a straight tape read with no fundamental work backing it

by the time the fundamentals justify the move that took place...half that shit is over

this is why u want deep familiarity, 5-10 years in the same sector

I haven't looked at something like Dillards in 8 years, 24-48 hours I'm current

whereas if you said "go learn Micron" I'm years away

once u understand a sector/industry, the financial statements pre-populate in your mind

this is how u counter the "invest first, investigate later"

like I have spent so many days of my life trading shit like apparel, u just develop familiarity with the way certain names trade

and newsflow hits, it gaps up 10%, and you've seen this movie so many times that ur gut says "buy it up 12%, now"

that response was created by the 4-5 times where I didn't buy it up 10%

weird subconscious shit that develops just staring at tape all day and all night

I run a few other screens too, all the sector ETFs like spdrs, plus the entire consumer cyclical subsector with mkt cap over $300m

prob takes 20-30 mins but over many years, u will silently upload info on reading the tape, what happens "under the hood"....how the S&P can be flat but there can be a sea change under the surface

I can't really explain why or how this works or why its worth doing, although if Druck is religious about grinding charts at 4:30 AM then there is prob some signal

I'll do a better job on these in an article but u should be good to go, and on Finviz, just play around with that screener and all the toggles and tabs

really great site, even when I'm paying for BBG I still just use finviz lol

BBG is too slow and clunky on a lot of shit, this site just zips

get used to just learning weird new tickers and chart patterns...whats this company, what do they do....ask LLMs and so on

a certain type of brain will go down this rabbithole without me telling them to

this is the shit that makes winners, winners

I hate to say it, because markets aren't the NFL

but it's the same principle...like, the guy who is putting in 1-2 hours daily, outside of work hours, grinding his P&L/blotter/losses, and grinding daily market action thru charts...

that shit compounds, everything compounds, over 5-10 years these daily efforts become jaw dropping

install these habits (and other good habits) and never break them, thats what determines success vs failure.....people with losing attitudes do not understand that every winner's story is this same sentence:

"A Ten-Year Overnight Success Story."

they see u in one day, on year 10, winning a title

they don't see the 10 years of staring at ur fucking losses every day

no one saw that

that was u, in a dark room, all alone

trying to fix what is broken in ur process, and what is broken within u as a man

u will discover that the two are the same

grab ur shovel and ur lunch pail...

because its hard hat szn🪖

good luck trading

tweets.text:
FAQ on "breaking down tape" for fundamental L/S -- why do it, what does grinding thru charts teach u, whats the framework/philosophy to understand, what are u looking to solve for, how does this aid u as fundamental analyst/PM, and how can LLMs help u master this?

Part 1 of 5: WHY

I. Helps answer Q: "What is the market telling us?"

II. Grinding thru charts each day after mkt close (or pre AM next day) helps develop pattern recognition, and understand interplay b/w news and px (and how this changes in various regimes --> can be used to spot regime changes)

III. useful for risk mgmt, entry/exit, avoiding trades driven entirely by momentum or buying "falling knives," also v useful for idea generation (longer topic)

IV. part of a disciplined rsch process, esp in a coverage model... grinding thru charts is how you spot individual names that seem dislocated or may have signals within unusual px action.

II. ORIGIN

1. this is not my creation, this was taught to me by a former PM (process was very similar to Druck's re: having an early-morning "chart pack" with hundreds of charts, 200-300 macro, all bonds/energy/commods and more) plus anywhere from 250 to 1500 U.S. equities -- usually 250-500

2. Many PMs are "chart first" the same way Steve Cohen is, or PTJ, or other trader-types...fundamentals matter to all of them, but even Druck says no fundamentals can make him buy an awful chart. this is just pragmatism/risk mgmt

3. I generally haven’t seen this practiced by many analysts, or written up online as "good practice" despite being fairly commonplace amongst L/S PM's - not sure why this is

4. Its most useful for anyone who has some grounding in fundamentals, but who needs to learn “market feel” - so even if u have banking/PE experience and are above-average on financial statement analysis, you start from zero here, just like everyone else.

III. PURPOSE

1. not just "what is the market telling us" but "what is the market regime RIGHT NOW, what is the current trend?" It doesn’t tell us what’ll happen tmw. Neither do fundamentals, if u havent noticed. Nothing does.... nothing "works," nothing is bulletproof.

2. However, momentum is the most powerful force in markets, and understanding today, is not going to hurt in thinking abt what happens tmw. Also, helps develop an understanding of mkt regimes and narrative as primary drivers of px in short-term, as well as capital flows/liquidity, all of which are a very real part of the game.

3. In times like these where nothing makes sense (too many cross currents), too many opinions, too much noise…”dont read news, read tape.” The market always moves first – everything you read is downstream from this. If u are confused about the mkt right now the absolute worst thing you can do is scroll Twitter. 

4. Everyone here is repeating 3rd and 4th hand interpretations of tape from some other guy, or ignoring it entirely. 

How many tweets have you seen in the past 3-12 months "wow the market is being soooo stupid and offering great names down 20%, sharpen ur pencils boys," and now they're all down 50% with the SPX at record highs, not once asking "maybe the market is right and I'm wrong?" 

Point being, just go right to the tape urself and form ur own opinion...is the tape perfect, no, nothing is, but its the best we've got. 

IV. PHILOSOPHICALLY

1. Capital duration dictates time horizon and thus reliance on px action. If you're Buffett, you don't care about charts as much (if at all) as 99.9% of asset mgmt. If you're in multi-mgr L/S, px action matters and there's no way around it, as do sentiment, positioning, and so on. I am guessing you aren't working at Berkshire Hathaway and so charts will help with all things px action.

2. Paying attention to single-stock eps reactions (which you'll see breaking down tape) helps gauge underlying health of a stock, a sector, and as a broad mosaic, the market

3. When u are learning a new stock, study the last 10-20 years of the chart, u want to know everything that happened, all the big moves, and what drove them (bc history doesnt repeat but it always rhymes). If a stock has gapped 30% on earnings multiple times, it can and will happen again...some businesses are more conducive to these moves than others.

4. Druck quote: “the single best forecaster of the economy is the inside of the stock market.” Inside meaning, internals (longer topic), sector rotation, leadership, breadth, lots of "under the hood" measures... not just what the SPX does each day. 

V: HOW I LEARNED

1. When I say "mentorship," there usually is no such thing. A PM wont be looking over your shoulder. If you're in the same room as them and get to listen to them as they think thru shit, you are very lucky, and that's a true mentorship even if its indirect.

2. The best mentor is a crazy motherfucker bc they talk to themselves out loud all day. This is an A+ seat if u land it. I’m crazy fwiw so crazy is a term of endearment.

3. These chart packages had to be ready around 5-530 AM, printed out, on his desk, which was when he walked in. Youngest guy on desk had to do this which was me at the time. So that meant being in very very early swapping names in and out of various packs, updating "current positions" chartpack, and so on.

4. After doing this every day for years, it naturally became a part of my process, you just get used to knowing how every single name you cover is trading (in my case consumer). Only difference is that some PM's prefer to do this pre-mkt, I'd rather stay late and spend 30 min anytime between 4-8 PM grinding thru charts...mornings always have enough going on.

after 10-15 yrs of doing this daily, "breaking down tape" compounds and u end up with better market feel than other ppl u know.

NEXT STEPS:

I originally wrote this template up FAQ style/organized bc I was gonna do a video on it, but honestly, I'm posting it here bc I think u are going to be better off with our good old friends the clankers.

Using LLMs for Mastery: you can ask LLMs abt this just as you would anything else...you want to learn/understand:

high level
>market internals
>understand sector rotation, cyclicals vs defensives
>understand mkt leadership (broad vs thin), breadth
>understand breakouts and breakdowns and what they signify
>understand volume and gaps
>understand incremental buyers and sellers, liquidity,  outsized effect on price when a stock is crowded into a trend reversal, muted effect on prices when a stock is "sold out" / capitulation

idea gen
>understand relative strength and weakness, not the technical indicators like RSI, but just eyeballing "this stock trades unusually well compared to sector/index"

>understand how during a market selloff, to find the stocks that are trading the best / showing signs of institutional support. these will be the leaders of the next leg higher (long idea gen).

>this works in reverse as well. right now the SPX is 1% off all time highs. if some high beta dogshit is already down 40-50%, and then the entire market rolls over, the names that were weak in a strong tape will lead to the downside in a bearish tape (short idea gen).

[aside: risk mgmt/current tape]
>with all these charts...u want to understand how to LISTEN TO THE TAPE.

>I have to just comment with ES/NQ rolling over rn, there has been so little humility on display its incredible. I have seen 1000 tweets where someone is sitting on a (55%) loss and will just laugh and say "oh yeah, this stock disconnected from fundamentals a loooong time ago -- can you believe how silly this is, clearly manipulated." 

>Like holy shit. Zero possibility in their mind that they are wrong, haven't cut any losses, haven't sold a single share of stock...ask an LLM about this, I can't, I literally can't.

>this is not a "disconnected" tape, nor is it a "factor" tape, the market is razor fucking sharp right now on separating winners vs losers, repricing them in in real-time as incremental newsflow arrives, and reallocating mkt cap accordingly. 

>I don't even like commenting on current moves like this, and I never wish red P&L on anyone (horrible karma), its just hard watching new ppl learn old lessons, and confirmation bias puts a man in what is really a jaw-dropping state of delusion

>not semis (they've been riding a multi-yr winning trend) but all rest of tech...if u didn't sell a share down 10%, 20%, 30% or 40%, and now ur at 50-60% and still refuse to believe u may be missing something? Lord...

>general rule, when the index is printing record highs and your stock is down some 20%, first instinct should be stop out --> ask "am I missing something" --> reunderwrite from scratch. you can always buy it back. you rarely will.

Just listen to the tape, that's the point of all this, at least entertain what it may be telling u...down 50% with the index @ record highs is a position u should never end up in.

arcana
>with all of this, always ask "how can this practice help me as fundamental analyst" + how can it be part of my process, etc

>avoid going too deep into technical-analysis land, this isn't meant to be that. this is additive to a fundamental analyst process

>no L/S idea gen should ever have shit like stochastic oscillators or MACD or moving averages in it

>everything is two-sided in markets - if a stock is ramping higher, one man sees a mean-reversion trade, the other sees a momentum trade, and both could be right. thats why u keep this shit out of ur idea gen

>at the end of the day this is all sort of "arcana." The no-mans land, the DMZ, between fundamentals/technicals...ur looking for unusual px action that could signal an inflection in fundamentals.

--

Overall: FORM YOUR OWN OPINION. In fundamentals, go right to the source docs, and in reading tape, go right to the charts. 

The LLM post is below bc this is all another part of one's education, so just plug everything written above into that framework.

I'll link a few other posts below this on fundamentals/technicals + grinding charts.

good luck trading, be humble, listen to the tape, and USA (Use Stops Always).

quotedTweet.text:
on unit growth stories - example frameworks/templates to add to this, ways to think abt modeling

7-8 part tweet

I spend an ungodly amount of time on store builds and the 1000 diff ways to think abt/model productivity, white space, value of store base at maturity discounted back...and so on

I think ppl will see that thread below and say "I need some inputs to get to his output." 

I'll give u some

confidence isn't found in one method. its when u have 50 diff methods that all converge, that all say "the answer is around x." 

this is how each new method increases the aggregate confidence interval.

because, from an analytical rigor standpoint, they SHOULD all align. 

a store does X revenue at Y margin and produces Z profit. 

if those #'s aren't somewhat constant, u have something misplaced or misaligned in ur view of economic reality.

1. INTRO

the incremental store, the value driver -- will LLMs be able to help get that right? 

hell if I know. probably. but typically all of the key drivers in there, the 1-3 that u decide matter, they come from:

I. primary research (#1 by far)

II. stress-testing mgmt's estimates of unit economics from their deck/transcripts...they can be lazy, sloppy, obsolete.

so you're constantly breaking down new qtrly info and collapsing into unit-level EBIT, ROIC, ROIIC and so on.

u will find that mgmt's old deck says "we get 25% cash-on-cash" and new boxes are doing 20%. or labor or store-level cogs/opex has changed in the last few months.

the trajectory of new store economics drives the stock

III. historical results (sometimes u break down and rebuild ur model in a new way that reveals some insight or reflects economic reality better)

2. LLM's and "the incremental store"

there's definitely ways to leverage LLM's to forecast how "the incremental store" in Knoxville will do, the amt of data u have relative to a Google search is unlimited

get the address of the new store and then learn everything about the 5 sq mi around it, traffic, comps, privates, there's so much that could flow into a model.

so I don't know, no one does, but the "100th store slowdown" short framework is reasonable, and its one of many. 

sometimes the puzzle is: can they do 1000, 1500 or 2000 stores in the US? stock could double or get cut in half on that

everything is on "the incremental store," and the economics of that store.

--

3. good habits

brett is the man for 5 things that I have to point out, random analyst musings

a. thinking out loud constantly even if only 50% baked. 

stuff good analysts do which stick out like a sore thumb on twtr, where everyone wants to appear certain and confident. paradoxically, the ppl just throwing shit at the wall w/ no conclusion, are the ones who know their shit

b. willingness to go way out of his element and just figure something out re: guardrails, dimensions, frameworks in modeling

sign of a highly experienced analyst and just comes from looking at 10,000 different companies

prob takes 10+ years. younger analysts get stuck "how do I do this, its not disclosed, etc."

but your job is to figure it out. in that case, the "100-store wall," all the moving parts to get to store 100, and then breaking it all down into model-able variables

plus ones u could potentially diligence (demographics/income etc)

if u said "go model this Mongolian iron ore smelter" or "a chain of japanese jerkoff parlors" or something random, a really good analyst just starts flying around. 

also if that japan chain exists its worth 50x, every single japanese tweet is either about American BBQ or wanking. some MBA grads with search fund $$ need to get over there and run the SBUX/CMG or even WING playbook

c. mountains of variables

the answer to "how do I do this" is to just start hurling paint on the canvas and see what emerges as u do, and iterate

literally everything is work in progress, u dont sit and think, u think via action

so even though brett isnt a resto analyst you see him just slapping all these different variables together, which could be paired and flexed in a million diff permutations

this actually gets much easier once you go out-of-sector and realize all businesses are the same; volumes and price, fixed and variable. you may lose some nuance but can get a functional unit-level model pretty fast 

d. in LLM'ifying all of this

I have no aptitude for this stuff yet but again, brett is just taking #2 and using it for #3.

the work is #2, what drivers/variables to use. translating that to LLM is the less-taxing part mentally.

I don't think ppl understand the % breakdown between modeling and LLM

younger guys might just go direct to LLM "build me a model" then tweak that

one store

tweets.text:
the only thing abt thinking in "book of base rates" or blackjack terms, for markets, is that u cant overlook the magnitude of the tail outcome

this is the same error that has blown up everyone at least once, taken major firms down, etc

Bessent talks about how Russia defaulting in the late 1990's was literally a 0% probability

but, prob should've been modeled as .0001%

and then u have the magnitude of the .0001% outcome, paired with the leverage of an LTCM, and game over

ditto gamestop

this is where the blackjack analogy or even pari-mutuel one fail to capture "think in expected value terms," markets have a far wider range of outcomes

like a capital structure with $50M of equity and $2B of debt, you could play 99 of 100 hands betting that the equity goes to zero and win

its that final step that ppl miss, the outcome of the 1/100 hand...its not a 2x or 3x, the magnitude of the tail outcome is like a 10x or 100x

feels like a "u can only learn this the hard way" lesson but in the future, u will at least reflect back on this post, like...oh, I see what he meant now.

quotedTweet.text:
for L/S, there is something to be gained in thinking about process the same way you'd think about a blackjack system

because u are taking lots of shots and relying on the law of large numbers -- over say 10,000 hands -- to where process and outcome should converge

(1/6) - this is especially true in multi-mgr where u might have 50 names, each of which present say 10 events/catalysts per year

so as an analyst, that's 500 shots

in blackjack, basic strategy reduces the house edge from 2-5% to less than 1%...basic strategy being the systematic model which dictates ur best move based on ur cards + the dealer upcard

and so in a L/S seat where ur taking tons of shots, u want to gradually strip out discretion where possible, in the quest to make ur process consistent and repeatable

even Buffett, despite being "qualitative" as a fundamental biz analyst, is pretty systematic in how he goes about shit. his decision making process is more akin to a gigabrained probability-calculation machine than a human being.

experience teaches u that there's a sliding scale of discretionary vs systematic, and esp in risk mgmt or sell discipline, u want to automate + remove emotion

but the exact calibration of the scale, the right % of discretion, that's a lifelong adjustment process and specific to u.

this is why blackjack is useful as a mental model. I think Munger prefers pari-mutuel betting/horseracing as the analogue, bc the payoffs are more reflective of how markets price assets, but both work (as does poker).

2.

as for the "basic strategy" of markets, it would be whatever mix of variables comprise winning process for u...no clear definition/many possible inputs.

i.e. understanding ur "circle of competence," ur style, and identifying the setups where u consistently are able to extract dollars from the market

lots of tiny details which u can only learn thru trial and error

but this is how ur odds improve from the standard 50-50 coin flip proposition

meaning...if u or me or a monkey throwing darts showed up, picked a random ticker, and blindly clicked "buy" or "sell," we theoretically should all begin with the same 50-50

3. 

the main difference is that in markets, u have a much wider variance in batting/slugging

some of the greatest managers ever, like Soros or PTJ, are only right 30-40% of the time

but their low win rate/batting average, is offset by their winners being much larger in size than their losers.

in simple numbers: if u can get a win rate of 51%, just north of even, and have your wins be 2x the size of your losses...u are going to be one of the greatest money managers of all time.

over 10,000 trades, ur annualized return/CAGR will be about 50%.

if u assume 1,000 trades per year, over 10 years your equity will 50x... $100,000 turns to $5 million.

4. 

will u have a 51% win rate, probably not

this is simply to illustrate that u only need a tiny edge + bigger wins than losses + large sample size, for a system to generate crazy LT returns.

if u assume a 40% win rate with the same ratio (reward = 2x risk), ur annualized return is 19% -- about the same as Buffett.

but if u reduce the ratio to 1.5x, meaning ur wins are 1.5x the size of ur losses, ur returns on a 40% hit rate collapse to breakeven (~0% annualized return).

u can fuck around with the math all u want, but the only way any of this becomes reality is by taking thousands and thousands of shots, year after year

this is the first step, figuring out where u have the highest hit rate, with the second step being risk mgmt, sell discipline, cutting losses fast and letting winners run

5.

the most important takeaway from all this, is that everything starts and ends with "breaking down tape"

u cannot know what ur good at without staring at ur historical P&L/trade blotter

and there have to be a lot of reps in there for signal to emerge from noise

so go pay ur "tuition," the only way u learn markets is thru thousands of reps and years of generating red P&L

until u have losses to study, u don't have shit

this all applies for building models as well. u gauge the efficacy of a model by whether it correctly forecasts earnings

if u arent measuring ur forecasts vs actual, measuring ur process vs the outcome, u are just wasting ur time

that's what the 2x2 matrix below is for -- process vs outcome -- those four possible squares encompass every trade or investment result, and they tell u where u need to devote ur time.

otherwise, u aren't iterating. nothing is getting done. u don't know what's luck and what's skill, and u really have no clue if what u are doing in general is right or dead wrong.

6.

above all, u gain absolutely nothing from scrolling twtr

scrolling only leads to ppl having 1,000 new ideas each day, software, oil, gold, and asking 1,000 dumb ass questions where I give the exact same answer:

"what does ur P&L say?"

all the answers u seek are in your red P&L

if u understand the self-improvement process via trial & error -- as in, take shots, analyze ur mistakes, iterate off them, and repeat -- there is a 0% chance u are DMing me or anyone else

none of us have a clue if u should buy software

u will only learn if u should, by doing it 100 times and studying ur P&L. everything is trial by fire

asking ppl about 1000 new trade ideas only says "I'm not serious about markets" or "I'm afraid of putting $ at risk" or something else that just feels wrong

either the hunger and the passion are missing, or the mind is just dialed to a different frequency.

END

before experience, there is def an attitude/mindset that is conducive for all this, and its visible at a young age

there is a lot of informational content in this quote from Steve Cohen on evaluating trader talent: "I'm looking for people who are not afraid to take risks. One of the questions I ask is: "Tell me some of the riskiest things you've ever done in your life." I want guys who have the confidence to be out there; to be risk takers."

that's exactly it...not specific to him at all, look at a Druck or Soros or Tepper, look at Buffett/Munger, all their track records are built off slugging + riding winners in monstrous stomach-churning size.

if u embrace risk, u will be dying to test ur ideas in the market with $ attached, or at least, ur competition will be

versus just going thru the motions of doing stock pitches and models, listening to business podcasts all day, reading too much business news, other pointless business bullshit with no tie to P&L

if u just want to "talk stocks" without any cost basis or P&L attached, then go tweet all day, that's what 99.9% of ppl are here for

but stop wasting ppl's time pretending like ur serious 

why would anyone want to critique pitches where u never have a single dollar behind any of them...if u have no conviction in ur ideas, if u clearly don't care, no one else is going to care either.

esp when ur competition consists of psychopath mf's who are foaming at the mouth

ultimately the best feedback u will get on a pitch will always come directly from the market -- particularly in the form of red P&L

so if u actually want to improve, take some risk for fucks sake

a man named jim simons has some advice for u...u may have heard it before, it's his #1 recommended way for someone to learn investing.

"Go short some wheat and see how it feels."

good luck trading

great man bios, heroes, conquerors, leaders, all the way back to the Greeks and Romans

u want to build relationships with them, where u develop their collective voices in ur head, and let their advice be what guides u through life.

I didn't understand this until say 35 but it could've been useful at 25

3/5

uploading the "eminent dead" is how u become a leader and exercise independent judgement, rather than blindly following the crowd

u will quickly realize that most people have no fucking clue what they're doing, a lot of opinions are just mechanically repeating what they were told

if u ask ppl "why do u believe what u believe?" they freeze up

and in following the footsteps of the eminent dead, u will recognize that there is a wide divergence in what they would do vs. what the crowd u see around u is doing..."this isn't right, this isn't how all the heroes throughout history would act."

everything great comes from having courage in ur own convictions + from a willingness to say, "I see everyone going that way, but I know that the correct thing to do is go this way"

over time, people will pick up on that u have some clue what ur doing, and they will start following u

4/5

on social media, u mostly want to leave this shit alone

all it does is slopbeam "crowd habits" into ur brain rather than the habits of the eminent dead, which u would get from books

these forums are best used for getting "reps" in writing, in creativity, evaluating ur ideas, and getting feedback

stay as far away as possible from the gossip section, or passing judgment on random finance/tech "celebrities" who u will never meet and have no bearing on ur life

when ur young, u will see the crowd doing it and u will blindly do what the crowd does so u can "fit in"

u will make an anonymous account and talk about how stupid terry smith is, despite that he runs 12 billion, and ur unemployed daytrading a $25k robinhood account

as u read more u will see that the Eminent Dead are unanimous on critics...loathed, held in contempt, viewed as cowards, and criticism in general is viewed as a massive waste of time, i.e. "great minds talk about ideas, small minds talk about people"

when u look back at the time u spent engaging in it, u will realize they were right. u never gain anything in bringing others down, every single minute is an 100% pure waste of time 

u will learn that u can read people very quickly based on what they talk about, because people talk about what they think about, and people think about whatever they upload

for some that's books, for others its gossip

but for all, the output will always reflect the input... because "what you focus on expands."

5/5

as long as u block off these weekly hours, and u keep a stack of 10 books around, ur gonna be good

u can have several genres going - few novels, few bios, few history books, few psychology/philosophy, etc

because ur mood will change, ur attention span is variable, and some books require deeper concentration than others

biographies tend to be a heavier lift, whereas any novel written in the last 50 years... u can be tired and hungover and still rip through it

read what appeals to u, dont worry about what everyone else thinks, never force anything

some writers or individual titles inevitably just wont click for u

there's no rhyme or reason, I don't like Dickens, I don't like Dostoevsky, I like Tolstoy, I like some Thomas Mann, but not all....is this how it's "supposed" to be, I don't know and don't care

u read these books to try and figure out how this life shit actually works. there is no "supposed," a book is either helping u or it isnt

if one isn't working for u, just give it to a friend and keep starting new books until one "clicks," it always will

END

that's all there is to it

if u read a lot, u will never in your life know what "boredom" or "loneliness" feel like

every problem u will ever face, there is a book written on how to either solve it, or how to navigate it while keeping ur head about u

and if a book shifts ur worldview, and u suddenly recognize u have the wrong ppl around u, trust ur gut and change what needs to be changed

the eminent dead will never steer u wrong

will end this with a letter that John Adams wrote to his son:

--

"Read somewhat in the English poets every day. You will find them elegant, entertaining and instructive companions, through your whole life.

To one who has taste, the poets serve to fill up time which would otherwise pass in idleness, languor, or vice. You will never be alone, with a poet in your pocket. You will never have an idle hour.

How many weary hours have been made alert, how many melancholy ones gay, how many vacant ones useful, to me, in the course of my life, by this means?"

- J. Adams
Amsterdam, May 14th, 1781

The Soros-Druckenmiller dissension came to a head over VeriSign , an Internet-security company that the funds bought at $50 a share last year and rode to $258 by late February. At Mr. Druckenmiller's behest, the funds doubled their bet on VeriSign to $600 million in early March, after a visit by VeriSign Chief Executive Stratton Sclavos. The CEO wowed Soros executives with talk of what a pending acquisition of Network Solutions could do, say people familiar with the visit.

VeriSign was at $240 when Mr. Druckenmiller doubled up. As the Nasdaq quaked, the stock fell to $135 by early April. Mr. Soros told his deputy, "VeriSign is going to kill us. We should take our exposure down."

quotedTweet.text:
paragon (cont)

re: random DM q's, just highlighting more shit the pitch does well, starting at top

intro: format

esp "what abt format"

there is no format, anything goes really

fair question if ur young... u want it to look good

but lot of times, its just u and 1-5 people talking, for hours, the "format" isnt a thing except in an intvw

a lot of these VIC pitches are straight text and they're effective

generally though, I think a good north star is: a good pitch should be a LEAN 2 pages and every paragraph punches them in the face - put all the fluffy shit, tables, graphs after that

if u can write 2 pages of straight lasers like this, u can write text

but for 99% of analysts, this would've taken them 10-20 pages to get their point across (and not been nearly as good)

the only way you can write a "text model" like this is from having spent 500 hours staring at Excel, he clearly knew Noble, knew the assets, had familiarty with all this

note how there's no fat, there's no two-paragraph business description

not even "paragon sells rigs"

in one sentence u get the entire setup and it works

if u can write one sentence that good, then do it

u don't need all the formal "variant view" etc,

he does none of that, but its all included in there

best way to frame it is prob, "I have 7-8 paragraphs to make my point, what do I want to talk about in each one, how do I write this shit so hard and tight that by page 1.5 he's buying puts on his phone"

1. maint/growth capex, there's just no other way to have that level of conviction than 5-10+ years doing primary research on the subsector.

and not just developing variant view on maint/growth split, but "here's why mgmt's guide is wrong"

not important where he worked at the time other than, top-tier SM, europe based -- but thats rsch driven by both corp access + primary rsch

so if ur 20 years old u are not gonna write a pitch like this

tricky thing w/ maint/growth capex is u never know when you'll get paid, or if its priced...it affects FCF, but there's no catalyst that shifts mkt perception

esp bc maint capex isnt always disclosed

and then the pitch relies heavily on mgmt being idiots, which can go other way esp on short pitches (very easy to get hyperbolic), but I have no criticism here

but I wouldn't put like "they sounded dumb last transcript" as core of the pitch...its pretty clear that here, he just knows the whole space and how paragon sounds relative to rest (overly optimistic, poor operators)

so on maint/growth/fcf, how to think abt it re: event path, I don't know

but a pitch that goes right into fcf is never wrong, the guy that is fucking around with ebitda multiples is the one who is wrong

this is a far superior analyst to me, and prob 99% of people I've ever met, I blindly defer to him

you know what an ebitda based pitch doesn't take into account?

maint/growth capex

some dumbass prob was flexing 3x, 4x, 5x ebitda on this enterprise (bull or bear)

zero variant view

thats "average" analyst, this is a great analyst

2. all throughout the pitch just running down the ebitda to fcf math as variables

ebitda less capex less cash int less cash taxes gets u fcf

can default to that always, it works, its fundamentally sound, and u avoid messy/immaterial CFO stuff

cash int and cash tax wont change, u are just flexing ebitda and capex

and so as u analyze or adjust line items (revs, cogs, opex) ur right there

3. the rev components, most will go over the head of anyone who doesnt cover the space, but u can see rev = dayrates * utilization

its hard from the outside to see what drives his assumptions but idk if it matters

bc all throughout, he comes at ebitda from several angles.

the model might start at ebitda, a lot of models do (built out by segments, segment ebitdas all flow to main tab ebitda, and u flow down to EPS from there + use the same capex/cash int/cash tax as before, bang, FCF

when you know a company cold, that's what a 10+ year exp L/S analyst buyside model looks like

there's 3-4 variables that matter (as in this pitch) - the BS/CF, whatever

here, it prob goes to ebitda and then the rev math is a sanity check, with individual rigs broken out as a 2nd sanity check above revs

i've seen these models, they are a mess, u model all these individual rigs

but trying to flow 40 rigs into total rev is silly -- and all the warm/cold stacking, u model that, its GIGO

so something like this, esp where u are playing for a terminal outcome...

"better vaguely right than precisely wrong"

the way hes does it is great in the sense of, we have certainty in capex int and taxes to the point where ebitda being 400, 500, 600 or 800...u have a lot of room to be wrong

just constantly running bull/base/bear on everything as u go through it, and u dont even need to be laying it out fancy model style

here's base, if we sensitize x y we get z, other way we get zz

that's how you turn 1 page of text into 1 paragraph

10 page pitch should be 10 paragraphs, cut two, you have a lean 2 pager

4.  fcf

the fcf/dcf math is simple here and unfortunately not every stock is so easy to run in ur head

in any case here u only have a few years fcf remaining so u can sensitize it the way he does

i'm not sure i've seen a pitch on a stable company that could do a "paper dcf" I guess you could call it...if fcfs are predictable then you probably could

but the pitch is fundamentally sound...no P/E * EPS, like, these are the fcfs

mkts price off fcf, not eps

there's asset value for co's like these, he deads that angle and keeps going...the pitch pre-empts all the questions that a PM would ask

"could they do xyz"

a good short pitch has all the bull tenets available (from street) so if you can just take a machete and slice shit to pieces for 8 paragraphs, thats gonna be a good pitch

5. capital structure

almost absurd to read

this is one of those pitches where you are so far away from consensus, and from market pricing, that you have to wonder wtf you're missing

sitting there like "why isnt the market cap 0 right now, what could I be missing"

I'll tell you what you're missing

its called conviction, and an appetite for risk

they go hand in hand

but this is just a high-conviction pitch, like everything is sealed the fuck up

there are so few analysts who even have the balls to write a pitch like this, much less get it right

"the equity is a zero and the debt is a good short" is an outrageous bar

like u better nail this fucking call, because u are straddling the line on cocky vs confident

pitching a fucking equity short with such conviction that at the end, u sprinkle in that this equity is so fucked u can short the bonds

bygone era, u cant do that at a multi

and this pitch wouldnt exist at a multi...prob too illiquid I'm guessing

and you'd have to own something against this squiggly little levered equity turd

btw, if u look at the stock chart, I think this IPO'ed at $18 and went to $9

so imagine the chart

down 50% in a straight line

u walk in with ur pitch "short it down 50% because its going to zero, press it all the way down and also short the fucking debt"

if u are a L/S analyst, ur gut instinct shivered right there at the thought of shorting something after its off 50% in a straight line

too many scars from shorting something down 40% into a print and it goes up 50% on a miss

much less some shitco like this where the fundamentals are bad, but if the backdrop changes, this shitco equity stub will rip your fucking dick off

you see these 2-3x off the lows on just a small move in oil, crowded positioning, no real change in fundamentals

but thats it bro, I don't remember seeing any other VIC pitches that were as sharply written. everything about this would be fine as a multi-mgr pitch

most VIC pitches are snoozers, like NVR homebuilders

"we see book value compounding at 23% for the next 5 years"

useless in multi mgr L/S

end

somehow I forgot

the very first line being "price target = $0"

hero shit

courage and conviction are what separate an elite analyst like this from the rest, every PM will smile on these traits bc no one has them

u think some kid that just came from KKR to Millennium is gonna slam his dick on the table with a pitch like this

he doesnt know what "bid-ask" is yet

think thats it...if I missed anything DM.

tricky thing w/ maint/growth capex is u never know when you'll get paid, or if its priced...it affects FCF, but there's no catalyst that shifts mkt perception

esp bc maint capex isnt always disclosed

and then the pitch relies heavily on mgmt being idiots, which can go other way esp on short pitches (very easy to get hyperbolic), but I have no criticism here

but I wouldn't put like "they sounded dumb last transcript" as core of the pitch...its pretty clear that here, he just knows the whole space and how paragon sounds relative to rest (overly optimistic, poor operators)

so on maint/growth/fcf, how to think abt it re: event path, I don't know

but a pitch that goes right into fcf is never wrong, the guy that is fucking around with ebitda multiples is the one who is wrong

this is a far superior analyst to me, and prob 99% of people I've ever met, I blindly defer to him

you know what an ebitda based pitch doesn't take into account?

maint/growth capex

some dumbass prob was flexing 3x, 4x, 5x ebitda on this enterprise (bull or bear)

zero variant view

thats "average" analyst, this is a great analyst

2. all throughout the pitch just running down the ebitda to fcf math as variables

ebitda less capex less cash int less cash taxes gets u fcf

can default to that always, it works, its fundamentally sound, and u avoid messy/immaterial CFO stuff

cash int and cash tax wont change, u are just flexing ebitda and capex

and so as u analyze or adjust line items (revs, cogs, opex) ur right there

3. the rev components, most will go over the head of anyone who doesnt cover the space, but u can see rev = dayrates * utilization

its hard from the outside to see what drives his assumptions but idk if it matters

bc all throughout, he comes at ebitda from several angles.

the model might start at ebitda, a lot of models do (built out by segments, segment ebitdas all flow to main tab ebitda, and u flow down to EPS from there + use the same capex/cash int/cash tax as before, bang, FCF

when you know a company cold, that's what a 10+ year exp L/S analyst buyside model looks like

there's 3-4 variables that matter (as in this pitch) - the BS/CF, whatever

here, it prob goes to ebitda and then the rev math is a sanity check, with individual rigs broken out as a 2nd sanity check above revs

i've seen these models, they are a mess, u model all these individual rigs

but trying to flow 40 rigs into total rev is silly -- and all the warm/cold stacking, u model that, its GIGO

so something like this, esp where u are playing for a terminal outcome...

"better vaguely right than precisely wrong"

the way hes does it is great in the sense of, we have certainty in capex int and taxes to the point where ebitda being 400, 500, 600 or 800...u have a lot of room to be wrong

just constantly running bull/base/bear on everything as u go through it, and u dont even need to be laying it out fancy model style

here's base, if we sensitize x y we get z, other way we get zz

that's how you turn 1 page of text into 1 paragraph

10 page pitch should be 10 paragraphs, cut two, you have a lean 2 pager

4.  fcf

the fcf/dcf math is simple here and unfortunately not every stock is so easy to run in ur head

in any case here u only have a few years fcf remaining so u can sensitize it the way he does

i'm not sure i've seen a pitch on a stable company that could do a "paper dcf" I guess you could call it...if fcfs are predictable then you probably could

but the pitch is fundamentally sound...no P/E * EPS, like, these are the fcfs

mkts price off fcf, not eps

there's asset value for co's like these, he deads that angle and keeps going...the pitch pre-empts all the questions that a PM would ask

"could they do xyz"

a good short pitch has all the bull tenets available (from street) so if you can just take a machete and slice shit to pieces for 8 paragraphs, thats gonna be a good pitch

5. capital structure

almost absurd to read

this is one of those pitches where you are so far away from consensus, and from market pricing, that you have to wonder wtf you're missing

sitting there like "why isnt the market cap 0 right now, what could I be missing"

I'll tell you what you're missing

its called conviction, and an appetite for risk

they go hand in hand

but this is just a high-conviction pitch, like everything is sealed the fuck up

there are so few analysts who even have the balls to write a pitch like this, much less get it right

"the equity is a zero and the debt is a good short" is an outrageous bar

like u better nail this fucking call, because u are straddling the line on cocky vs confident

pitching a fucking equity short with such conviction that at the end, u sprinkle in that this equity is so fucked u can short the bonds

bygone era, u cant do that at a multi

and this pitch wouldnt exist at a multi...prob too illiquid I'm guessing

and you'd have to own something against this squiggly little levered equity turd

btw, if u look at the stock chart, I think this IPO'ed at $18 and went to $9

so imagine the chart

down 50% in a straight line

u walk in with ur pitch "short it down 50% because its going to zero, press it all the way down and also short the fucking debt"

if u are a L/S analyst, ur gut instinct shivered right there at the thought of shorting something after its off 50% in a straight line

too many scars from shorting something down 40% into a print and it goes up 50% on a miss

much less some shitco like this where the fundamentals are bad, but if the backdrop changes, this shitco equity stub will rip your fucking dick off

you see these 2-3x off the lows on just a small move in oil, crowded positioning, no real change in fundamentals

but thats it bro, I don't remember seeing any other VIC pitches that were as sharply written. everything about this would be fine as a multi-mgr pitch

most VIC pitches are snoozers, like NVR homebuilders

"we see book value compounding at 23% for the next 5 years"

useless in multi mgr L/S

end

somehow I forgot

the very first line being "price target = $0"

hero shit

courage and conviction are what separate an elite analyst like this from the rest, every PM will smile on these traits bc no one has them

u think some kid that just came from KKR to Millennium is gonna slam his dick on the table with a pitch like this

he doesnt know what "bid-ask" is yet

shout out to anyone who has stopped caring entirely about being liked

stuff u learn at 40, which would've been nice to know at 25... yet could not be known ex ante.

why?

because u don't know who ur friends are at 25.

once u nail that down... u should naturally arrive at this destination.

1/5

u take a look around, grateful, having come to understood two things:

I. loyal friendship is one of life's most beautiful blessings

II. loyal friendship is rare

after u read enough old books, u recognize that having 5-10 loyal friends over the course of one's lifetime would be outrageously good luck.

u count ur blessings, u stop chasing what u dont have, and u grow infinitely more grateful for what u do.

it's almost like coming out of a haze

2/5

u look at your 1000 social media "connections," u recognize that there's nothing for you there

u have enough friends where u can completely stop caring, from a position of strength, of peace, and of plenty

u would always prefer to be liked than to be hated.

and u know that the wise man avoids incurring hatred wherever possible.

but ultimately...u just don't care.

u feel driven by an obligation to pay it forward and be helpful to the younger versions of urself, just as others helped you 15 years ago

whether u are liked or hated is irrelevant to fulfilling this obligation

3/5

strangely, by expending 0 energy on being liked, u may end up with better results.

a wonderful example of this is John Adams' defense of the British

taking the course of action that he KNEW was going to lead to bloodcurdling hatred leveled in his direction.

this is why u cannot care about being liked or disliked, thats not ur north star...courage is

the great man finds himself at a crossroads frequently... remain silent and be liked, or do what he knows to be right, and give it no further thought beyond that

if u read history, u know that posterity will always vindicate the correct decision....that's your time horizon, not whether it's liked today.

4/5

last is losing all desire to fit in

this, again, is driven by the "eminent dead"

it appears binary to me every time

"u can either fit in, or u can be great."

u are either walking a crowded path into the crowd, or walking your own path into the forest.

the "lone wolf" archetype that Munger uses for himself

not to be confused with a misanthrope

people, in my experience, when u get them 1 on 1 behind closed doors...are universally good.

you can have a warm heart, a tight inner circle, a very high bar for ur time, and a preference for solitude -- all simultaneously.

5/5

with all of this, u aren't actively trying to not fit in, or to fit in

u just don't care

u tend to have no idea where u are relative to everyone else's opinion

u may be 100% in-line or 100% at odds

because this is the way.

think of how Buffett values a business on its own, with no market inputs.

END

here is a worldview that I feel is healthy and balanced

>the great man thinks critically and independently
>groupthink and crowdthink are toxic pollutants
>the mind is fertile soil and extremely sensitive to the inputs u feed it
>feeds and scrolling are poison, and u feel them destroying ur critical thinking capability

u simply have to protect your serenity, and it takes an active effort to preserve your peace. Nietzsche in this tweet below arrives at a similar conclusion

if I had to sum this entire approach up, I would say:
>u want to blend solitude and desire for independence
>u do not aim to be in or out, liked or disliked, and at all times, u retain a warmth and gentleness towards your fellow man as well as a desire to be of service with what little wisdom u possess
>u hold a polite and respectful apathy for the view of the crowd, and u do not aim to be in or out...your view is developed independently first, and may or may not dovetail with theirs second.

lot in there, my friend...I hope it at least helps u in thinking differently.

many high level and operating system changes one could make -- starting with yourself, and then the way u approach life, the crowd, society, and your fellow man.

whatever u do, "never let ur warm heart turn cold."

(process vs. outcome) + (means vs. ends)

These two parallel ideas in mkts and life have to be understood

esp in markets, this is "major brain re-wire" territory

this is a lot more about attitude than anything else

1. in life, the moral precept is that the ends don't justify the means.

that's the "should" of how life should work...reality is more complex unfortunately:

i.e. "why do good men suffer while wicked men prosper?"

that's the same conundrum as ends/means

"my good means are getting me bad ends, and his wicked means are getting him good ends, wtf?"

that's life. but no philosophy for this post rn

just accept the moral precept of "ends dont justify means."

2. HOWEVER...markets are more nuanced.

I have not seen this made as a declarative statement, but I suspect that it would get the "yup" from the market sages and wise men:

"In markets, outcomes justify process."

A process is a good process if it generates winning outcomes.

The question with no answer, the nuanced part, is "what is the correct time horizon?"

3 years, 5 years, 7 years, 10 years?

When can you comfortably state that "these outcomes are driven by a consistent, repeatable process" as opposed to "a monkey throwing darts?"

A long time ago I uploaded 7 years as the answer, lost the source, but 7 years is the length of an average market cycle.

This means u get to see how a guy trades a bull market and a bear market. Until u have seen someone trade both, they haven't proven themselves.

You need the levered bull market geniuses to get wiped, and the overly conservative cash hoarders to underperform.

Whoever is left standing after that, with a solid-looking 7-year track...real-ass motherfucker, made man, O.G.

That logic is still sound to me, but I think the time horizon has shrank to 3-5 years, maybe less bc of how short a multi-mgr time frame is

or because more reps + more trades + more data to evaluate process/outcome = shorter required duration for the same amount of data...I don't know and the answer is clearly fluid anyway.

3. "Outcomes justify process."

I had to add the nuance at the beginning clarifying that this is not equivalent to means vs. ends

This is why people avoid making it declarative

But this is so important to understand from an attitude/mindset perspective

People who are results-focused, performance-focused, outcome-focused...just a different breed of human, winning attitude, same mindset as athletics

It's not nature, it's nurture

I know for a fact because ages 0-21 I had nothing going for me

You can take anyone and with 3-4 years of amazing mentorship, hazing really, u can turn a kid or a young man into a competitor, a legit human

I think that's why I feel so strongly about ages 20-25, like, I am just such a believer that in man's ability to destroy and rebuild himself at will, infinite malleability, the fact that u can become an entirely different person with 6-12 months of work

But this is just how people in any seat with P&L responsibility communicate

Twitter is not the real world, at all, I cannot emphasize this strongly enough

Go get coffee with the most high-powered person u can reach, somebody way up, and pay attention to everything about how they communicate

Like, day one, it's just made extremely clear by mentors, and then daily, by the market.

4. "This is not a career for people who make excuses."

That's basically it...because you are your P&L.

If you're down 20%, you are down 20%...like in the NFL, you are your record.

There is no "I'm down 20% but I'm good at this"

A good mentor will just wring this out of you immediately, like "you're down 20%, just shut the fuck up until your P&L doesn't suck."

There is no blame, 100% of everything falls on your shoulders

Ownership, accountability, responsibility

"I'm wrong" "I fucked up" 500 times a day

There's no such thing as "it's the market's fault"

Stuff like that is how you get dinged or fired, these are old trading floor rules from when all the world's best talent was on bank prop desks

I don't know if "military" is the right word, but it's not far off

5. No one cares about your process if your outcomes suck

If you have P&L to your name, "shut the fuck up until you perform" is not even rude or offensive, it's just a fact

Don't talk until you've earned the right to talk

Show ur outcomes, show ur P&L... that's what determines whether u should be talking

Until then, why are u talking at all? Why are u worrying about some other guy's P&L when yours is trash?

These are logical queries, this is not shit-talk...like, sit down and explain your thought process

In general, if I think across powerful industries, people I can recall who were at the top, law, business, et cetera

like, people are extremely fucking blunt, the higher up you get

they don't have much time, and they have a million mf's asking for their time

it almost takes you aback at first because you expect a CEO or a guy with $500M to be out of the movies or something

You get 2 word texts and a 24 second phone call, and he moves a mountain for u...next

thats how u get to that level, thats how u move.

6. One team, one dream

I had a boss who followed me on twtr back in the day, it was noon and it was a slow day, I sent a tweet

Man blew my goddamn brains out

Why the fuck are you tweeting, look at the P&L you fucking jerkoff, look at your names, and tell me if u think u have earned the right to fucking tweet during market hours.

Boom, smoked my ass, and he was 100% on the money

I said "I'm wrong" for the 100th time, course-corrected and didn't do it again

It's not just me, I'm letting the team down and being disrespectful

This is all de rigeur and u don't mind someone checking you if your attitude is wrong. It's one team one dream, thats the sort military-ish aspect.

In real life, "shut the fuck up until u have earned the right to talk" is just the right way go about, well, pretty much everything

I have never encountered a valid counter-argument to it

It will serve you well literally everywhere you go

7. All-weather

All your life you will have guys 10-20 years older than you evaluating you, from 20 to 40, 40 to 60, and so on

First impressions and the way you carry yourself are probably far more of it than we can even appreciate

When you wire yourself to move a certain way, u don't have to worry about how u come off

I respect elders for their wisdom, try to treat everyone the exact same, I try to speak in fewer and fewer words each day, more silence, more action... words are straight up worthless, u learn it more and more every day.

That's all I know about life

On words, just stare at a guy when he's talking, ignore what he's saying, watch his face...and listen to what your gut is telling you.

Literally gives u the clearest possible read about someone

I don't know a word he said

I don't know what my gut said

But like Bruce Wayne, u felt as if a bright light got blasted across the night sky...the ratsignal.

8. Humble and quiet 

All these principles, are they good or bad, I don't know

Probably 90% books and mentorship, 10% confirmation thru life

Most are screwed in pretty tight, just because I have been a lot of fucking places, and never seem to have issues with the basic shit, communication, respect, humility, attitude

I believe this is because everyone likes the humble, quiet guy who believes in paying dues and prefers actions to words

And on the other end, everyone despises the guy who hasn't paid dues but won't stop talking

Every time I meet someone I really respect and admire, I note that they use as few words as possible

So that's the direction I'm going in...silence is good for the soul.

END: INSTALLATION

In general, it's a very very simple way of operating to understand, should be an easy install, I feel like if you went on YouTube and searched military shit, it won't steer you wrong

And then in business its just that, plus two things

-you get assigned work

[pause, think abt when u can have it done]

then respond: "I will have this for you Tuesday by 10 AM."

get them that shit Tuesday by 10 AM and make sure its the best thing they've ever seen in their life

do that over and over and just shut the fuck up otherwise, and u will be literally everyone's favorite person

"when I give him something, he tells me when it'll be back to me, I can check that off my list, I don't have to follow up with him, and when I get it back, that shit is flawless."

senior mgmt is just sitting there, talking about you for 10-15 minutes behind closed doors

"Do we want him as CEO, CFO or COO?"

all there is to it brotha

when ur 20, ur like, wow those guys must be superheroes

then at 40 you see which of your boys got tapped

they are good at three things and three things only...

1. execution
2. execution

you'll never guess the third

3. execution.

u know the drill...

do good work, get good bread 🍞

this is an excellent question, and one where I can give a serviceable answer for now

basically asking, "u tweet/write about breaking down tape, u post Kuechly breaking down tape...what is the market equivalent of this?"

I will try and keep it brief here, forgive rushed writing/typos

P&L:

going thru all ur losses and troubleshooting. process vs outcome, luck vs skill, learning from ur mistakes

this sounds very simple, and I sat down to write a tweet-length answer....4000 words later was like, oh shit

but this to me is the most important, its the #1 way to improve, people who are serious do it

and yet no one does it

2.

u want to know why 99.9% of people really don't do it?

they don't want to know the truth about themselves. the truth is ugly. they're afraid to look inside, because they don't know what they'll find.

and your P&L leaves you NOWHERE TO HIDE.

it is a mirror, and it's an unvarnished reflection of all your flaws, your bad decisions and your dogshit discipline

u cannot blame or make excuses, u cannot tweet around it, and it is immune to all forms of LARPitude

it's one of the clearest indicators of who is real not just as a trader but as a human

show me someone who is afraid to look at their P&L, and give me moneyline at -1000

lay $10k to win $1000 that they will never be successful in markets

its that simple

3.

if there were prop bets I'd tell u exactly how they blow their first account...time horizon, position sizes 

first off I've made every mistake myself, and second, over 10-15 years of trading, teaching friends/family, watching people fail in years 0-5 over and over and over...

I just know all the early-stage mistakes, especially the mental/cognitive ones, ego, vanity, denial, self-deceit, fear

someone in years 0-5 of trading markets is a fucking mess, like an asylum case...they underestimate how stupid, weak, and slippery the human mind is

4.

tell a guy "stop urself out down 20%" "okay"

takes a 60% loss

"what happened there chief? ur job was to see the number 20%, and then click the mouse....a 6-year old coulda done that"

mfs will either lose their shit, crumble, or enable some sociopath mode where the loss wasn't their fault

all people's fucked up childhoods and upbringings emerge in how they grapple with harsh truths

u see people who are knotted up too tight where u don't think they could ever be unwound

nothing is ever their fault, ever, and never will be

there are lots of people like this on twtr, in 2-3 sentences u can immediately discern how someone handles accountability and responsability

the human brain is frightening

so thats P&L.

1. grinding charts/running screens

I learned this from a boss back in the day, whose process wasn't too far off from this

Stan Druckenmiller: Okay, so every night, at about 4:30, I get 272 charts. They cover just about every group in the stock market, every commodity, every currency cross I'm interested, in every fixed income market around the world. And they're basically daily, weekly, and monthly. Daily supposed to predict 8-20 days, weekly 8-20 weeks, and monthly 8-20 months. When I make an investment decision, it's usually--sometimes, believe it or not: The idea comes from the charts, but I will never invest just on a chart. But if I really like a fundamental thesis and the chart stinks, I won't do it.

Druck trades macro, a L/S manager will have 500-1000 equity charts on top of that, diff time frames than Druck

you can do it post-close or pre-open

Druck and my boss were early AM, I always preferred doing it after the close

20-30 mins as a wind-down, just subconsciously uploading everything that happened during the day

here is a free screener I have always used

https://t.co/l8VF2TbITD

daily post-close, I do:

descriptive tab: "mkt cap > $300m"
technical tab: 52-week highs (1st screen) 52-week lows (2nd screen)

thats two diff screens, 52-week highs, and 52-week lows, both with $300m min (smalls mkt cap)

then, click "Charts" below all the toggles

this shows u where $ is sloshing in and out of, what's working, what isn't

u actually can use it for idea gen, because the market will always move first

before anyone has spilled a drop of ink, price has moved

everything is downstream of price

so when u see an odd move in a name that everyone has forgotten about, a name you knew well at one point, but that no one is talking about...

...and suddenly its printing 52w highs, on volume, on no news?

immediate "invest first and then investigate," in 24-48 hours you can get current

odds are always way better than 51-49 that fundamentals are inflecting, these trades are high hit rate because it's all incremental buyers from here

remember, no ink has been spilled yet

and there hasn't been any news

all u have is johnny-come-lately shorts getting taken out and the oddball deep value buyers, and now u prob have faster money, small L/S SM, prop desks, the minnows are there, the big fish

Druck talks about this but the fast, hard part of the move, is always when there's no news and no logic...u buy off instinct, bc u recognize the pattern, but u know that u are making a straight tape read with no fundamental work backing it

by the time the fundamentals justify the move that took place...half that shit is over

this is why u want deep familiarity, 5-10 years in the same sector

I haven't looked at something like Dillards in 8 years, 24-48 hours I'm current

whereas if you said "go learn Micron" I'm years away

once u understand a sector/industry, the financial statements pre-populate in your mind

this is how u counter the "invest first, investigate later"

like I have spent so many days of my life trading shit like apparel, u just develop familiarity with the way certain names trade

and newsflow hits, it gaps up 10%, and you've seen this movie so many times that ur gut says "buy it up 12%, now"

that response was created by the 4-5 times where I didn't buy it up 10%

weird subconscious shit that develops just staring at tape all day and all night

I run a few other screens too, all the sector ETFs like spdrs, plus the entire consumer cyclical subsector with mkt cap over $300m

prob takes 20-30 mins but over many years, u will silently upload info on reading the tape, what happens "under the hood"....how the S&P can be flat but there can be a sea change under the surface

I can't really explain why or how this works or why its worth doing, although if Druck is religious about grinding charts at 4:30 AM then there is prob some signal

I'll do a better job on these in an article but u should be good to go, and on Finviz, just play around with that screener and all the toggles and tabs

really great site, even when I'm paying for BBG I still just use finviz lol

BBG is too slow and clunky on a lot of shit, this site just zips

get used to just learning weird new tickers and chart patterns...whats this company, what do they do....ask LLMs and so on

a certain type of brain will go down this rabbithole without me telling them to

this is the shit that makes winners, winners

I hate to say it, because markets aren't the NFL

but it's the same principle...like, the guy who is putting in 1-2 hours daily, outside of work hours, grinding his P&L/blotter/losses, and grinding daily market action thru charts...

that shit compounds, everything compounds, over 5-10 years these daily efforts become jaw dropping

install these habits (and other good habits) and never break them, thats what determines success vs failure.....people with losing attitudes do not understand that every winner's story is this same sentence:

"A Ten-Year Overnight Success Story."

they see u in one day, on year 10, winning a title

they don't see the 10 years of staring at ur fucking losses every day

no one saw that

that was u, in a dark room, all alone

trying to fix what is broken in ur process, and what is broken within u as a man

shout out to anyone who has stopped caring entirely about being liked

stuff u learn at 40, which would've been nice to know at 25... yet could not be known ex ante.

why?

because u don't know who ur friends are at 25.

once u nail that down... u should naturally arrive at this destination.

1/5

u take a look around, grateful, having come to understood two things:

I. loyal friendship is one of life's most beautiful blessings

II. loyal friendship is rare

after u read enough old books, u recognize that having 5-10 loyal friends over the course of one's lifetime would be outrageously good luck.

u count ur blessings, u stop chasing what u dont have, and u grow infinitely more grateful for what u do.

it's almost like coming out of a haze

2/5

u look at your 1000 social media "connections," u recognize that there's nothing for you there

u have enough friends where u can completely stop caring, from a position of strength, of peace, and of plenty

u would always prefer to be liked than to be hated.

and u know that the wise man avoids incurring hatred wherever possible.

but ultimately...u just don't care.

u feel driven by an obligation to pay it forward and be helpful to the younger versions of urself, just as others helped you 15 years ago

whether u are liked or hated is irrelevant to fulfilling this obligation

3/5

strangely, by expending 0 energy on being liked, u may end up with better results.

a wonderful example of this is John Adams' defense of the British

taking the course of action that he KNEW was going to lead to bloodcurdling hatred leveled in his direction.

this is why u cannot care about being liked or disliked, thats not ur north star...courage is

the great man finds himself at a crossroads frequently... remain silent and be liked, or do what he knows to be right, and give it no further thought beyond that

if u read history, u know that posterity will always vindicate the correct decision....that's your time horizon, not whether it's liked today.

4/5

last is losing all desire to fit in

this, again, is driven by the "eminent dead"

it appears binary to me every time

"u can either fit in, or u can be great."

u are either walking a crowded path into the crowd, or walking your own path into the forest.

the "lone wolf" archetype that Munger uses for himself

not to be confused with a misanthrope

people, in my experience, when u get them 1 on 1 behind closed doors...are universally good.

you can have a warm heart, a tight inner circle, a very high bar for ur time, and a preference for solitude -- all simultaneously.

5/5

with all of this, u aren't actively trying to not fit in, or to fit in

u just don't care

u tend to have no idea where u are relative to everyone else's opinion

u may be 100% in-line or 100% at odds

because this is the way.

think of how Buffett values a business on its own, with no market inputs.

END

here is a worldview that I feel is healthy and balanced

>the great man thinks critically and independently
>groupthink and crowdthink are toxic pollutants
>the mind is fertile soil and extremely sensitive to the inputs u feed it
>feeds and scrolling are poison, and u feel them destroying ur critical thinking capability

u simply have to protect your serenity, and it takes an active effort to preserve your peace. Nietzsche in this tweet below arrives at a similar conclusion

if I had to sum this entire approach up, I would say:
>u want to blend solitude and desire for independence
>u do not aim to be in or out, liked or disliked, and at all times, u retain a warmth and gentleness towards your fellow man as well as a desire to be of service with what little wisdom u possess
>u hold a polite and respectful apathy for the view of the crowd, and u do not aim to be in or out...your view is developed independently first, and may or may not dovetail with theirs second.

lot in there, my friend...I hope it at least helps u in thinking differently.

many high level and operating system changes one could make -- starting with yourself, and then the way u approach life, the crowd, society, and your fellow man.

whatever u do, "never let ur warm heart turn cold."
