on using Twitter less / the eternal war against social media addiction

I've found it most helpful to have "Twitter days" and "non-Twitter days"

weekends, and then say Wednesday, are non-Twitter days

I know from experience that if I post something, it becomes a Twitter day

If I post something in the morning I somehow don't have the focus for reading books all afternoon/evening

I'm crazy grateful for the followers I have and genuinely enjoy engaging w/ people, idk how I got here but I feel like I'm bottom 5% percentile of intelligence...so many replies or DM's have me like, "how the FUCK are you so smart???"

nasty people and mean-spirited criticism is w/e, that scales linearly as u grow, u cant avoid them...check any big account...no amount of moral perfection can save u, they'll find something to denigrate.

the amount that u need to stare at ur feed "for work" is prob 1% true and 99% addiction/self-deceit/a negative esp for markets...think back to 2 weeks ago...guarantee u got sucked into consensus + groupthink and failed to make the correct play.

so... that leaves 4 "twitter days." the amount of ideas, tweets, articles etc that come to mind doesnt change - it actually grows on off-days (turn off ur phone for a day and watch ur creativity skyrocket).

this means you will end up posting a lot on those days. I ask myself: "is this a problem? the accounts I really like, do I care if they post a lot?"

honestly, no. this app is 99.9% garbage, slop, ragebait, engagement farming...I would say its the worst I've ever seen it and somehow continues to get worse, esp in times of war, where America's enemies know this is our weak point. why is Tucker Qatarlson Network in my feed pounding the table on Islam, really weird shit like that

so if you are a real human with something interesting to say, I have no problem with you flooding my feed, I'll read it all.

hopefully this helps. think back over the past 2-4 weeks of "monitoring the situation" and ask what it did for ya...NADA. zero or negative Return On Time.

read less tweets and more books

"I want to start posting and writing under my real name but I'm afraid what friends/family will think"

this is common and an age-old question

I'll pass along the best advice I've gotten or read on the subject, 3 things

first, you have to look back at every author in history and ask: "is this something they faced?"

the answer is obviously yes

its just a cost of doing business, price of entry, etc

this applies far less for business/self-help (bland, sterile) and more for the stuff worth writing about (life, pain, hardship) where u can really impact the readers life in a positive way.

2nd, on family...I've heard crazy stories (present-day) where a woman wrote a novel, like fantasy/fiction, totally innocuous, and her mother didn't speak to her for two years

I want to say "as long as you leave them out of it you should be okay" but its tricky bc if you think of some of the best books you've ever read...they took it there. "educated" by westover comes to mind.

the boilerplate advice seems to be "they'll get over it," which is true. family you're stuck with for better or worse, blood is blood.

3rd, on friends, I think this is the easiest part

if your friends don't support you putting yourself out there, get new friends.

sadly an old truism that "your friends want to do well...but not better than they're doing." 

La Rochefoucauld: "in our friends' misfortunes, we always find something not displeasing to us"

but you'll figure out real quick who is envious, toxic, negative, vs who is positive and supportive

the ones who mock you and try to chop you down...just smile and keep it moving.

as for the really good ones, if you lead by example, they'll follow you.

"a man's life comes in seasons" - no bad blood or ill will - as u start a new season, sometimes the cast of characters will change with it...que sera, sera.

put yourself out there. good luck 🫡

twitter needs more accounts like blueprint...really good attitude, humble, helpful, and incredibly self-effacing.

I just have to highlight what he said here bc its 100% accurate:

"differentiated himself by working 6 days a week with DCFs"

thats really all there is to it...I've never met someone from a top-performing team or firm (esp MM) that had a different answer.

-work 24/6 (ex-SAC thing that sundays are ~mandatory) 
-dcf focus and/or some ROIIC framework
-and then the 3rd sentence I'd add... "everything goes in my model." everything. heard that same phrase over and over

behind every curtain of "greatness" is just flawless execution, blocking, tackling, discipline...there is no magic bullet.

"sweat the small details until you have a puddle of perfection."

10 discarded prior notions on books & reading

1. "comparison is the thief of joy"

nature is aristocratic. benchmark urself to the best that humanity has produced (only a few great men/women per century), not ur neighbor, not random ppl on social.

what ur mostly seeing is fake and only part of a person...biographies/history show u, like the Tom Wolfe title, "A Man In Full."

2. "read quietly"

I say "trade quietly" a lot these days...keep all that shit to urself, anything social or external only introduces cognitive errors and biases.

same precept goes for reading, if ur reading to impress other people or to hit some random target ("50 books per year / 500 pages per day") ur prob reading for the wrong reasons

related:

3. read the same books over and over (every 5 years?)

books are to help u navigate life. sometimes a great day of reading might just be 5 pages, but where it set ur mind in motion, shifted ur worldview or led to a change in ur behavior

that's why u "read quietly"...who cares if u only read 5 pages of a book that u already read before. no one elses opinion matters

4. more than one at a time

theres nothing wrong with reading 5-10 books at once bc sometimes u just arent in the mood, or there's a light/heavy scale, some require more focused attention than others.

if u only do one, u may feel compelled to blast thru it and not retain anything just to get to another

5. some books or authors dont "click"

there are some authors that I seem to have a "mental block" with. I've read prob 4 dostoevsky books but dont remember a thing and found it painful from start to finish. meanwhile I've read tolstoy's War and Peace twice  and could easily go back for a 3rd

another one is dickens, I've never been able to get into a single one

I just don't care, I'll try back in 5 years but I'm fine with reality being that my mind just doesnt perfectly align with some authors...we're all unique in that regard

6. how books change your circle

imo two things change a man - books and experience

sometimes the combo of the two, will cause u to re-evaluate ur own beliefs, and u will recognize that u are surrounded by the wrong people...doesnt mean theyre wrong, just a misalignment between u and them

or that u no longer agree w/ a former mentor

thats all fine...walk ur own path. books are the best "north star" u will ever have

7. the best source of books to read is books that ur reading

most book recs are best found in books

example: munger always carried "a benjamin franklin" biography with him

if a bio tells u "napoleon took this plutarch book with him on his march to moscow" i'd add that book to ur list

if montaigne praises seneca and epicurus, i'd add those to your list

if lord chesterfield frequently quotes la rochefoucauld, i'd go there next

etc etc.  these are better signposts than asking Grok

8. why do old books survive

make sure u have a firm grip on why old books survive across generations

the sandstorm of history is powerful and obsolete or archaic books get buried very fast. I bet 99.9% of "the best books of 2026" have disappeared by 2126.

so when u see a book from 500-1000 years ago that is still relevant, i'd default to "there's probably something in here that is eternal about human nature" and rank it above something published yday

9. pace

a lot of the best books, whether old books, history or bios, can be thick

great biographies easily run 800+ pages

do not feel like there's a rush. knocking out 50 pages of a biography in a day requires pretty focused attention

so if TR's bio takes you 3 months, so be it. this is still a far better use of ur time than almost anything else.

10. no twtr on weekends

this is the only way to keep ur sanity and to get any reading done, the weekdays are just too hectic for the most part

turn this shit off, the ROI is zero and probably negative

if u dont have the discipline to obey a simple rule like "no twtr on weekends" that is actually a pretty serious problem....bc it means u wont have the discipline for much much bigger shit when the time comes.

--

He is negotiating through intimidation, signalling resolve, ruthlessness, and a willingness either to send Iran “back to the Stone Ages” or to ensure that “a whole civilization will die tonight” in terms that pierce the bubble of diplomatic euphemism and force the IRGC command to reassess its risk tolerance. In that sense, Trump is acting far closer to Machiavelli’s prince than to a modern liberal statesman: he is willing to appear vulgar, even “unhinged,” if doing so strengthens the fear of his threats in the minds of his adversaries.

What is striking is not that a leader dealing with such a regime would use this language, but that so many in the West seem genuinely unable, or unwilling, to recognize the strategy. 

They clutch their pearls about tone while ignoring the basic logic of coercive diplomacy: when you want to stop a hostile regime and its terrorist proxies from further escalation, you must shape their expectations, not placate your own commentariat. 

Machiavelli’s blunt counsel is that a prince must sometimes speak as both “man and beast,” combining law with the language of force to protect his people. One is left wondering whether our political and media classes have forgotten the oldest lessons of statecraft. Has no one read The Prince?

Plutarch's essay on "whether 'Live Unknown' is a wise precept" (from Moralia) is the best framework on how to think about your relationship with the world:

--

"For my part I should say, Even if your life be bad do not live unknown, but be known, reform, repent; if you have virtue, be not utterly useless in life; if you are vicious, do not continue unreformed."

"Our remote ancestors paid public attention to the sick, and if any one had either had or cured a similar complaint, he communicated his experience to the patient, and so they say medical art became great by these contributions from experience. We ought also in the same way to expose to everyone diseased lives and the passions of the soul..."

"...But nowadays people deny and conceal and cloak their vices, and so fix them deeper in themselves."

--

for some of you, this puts words to how you already felt - or at least it did for me.

I doubt I can convince anyone on the opposite side, but it can't hurt to try.

1/4

you can either be public or you can be anonymous ("Live Unknown").

you gain everything in being public. whatever you contribute is (ideally) useful to others and to humanity as a whole. 

at the same time, you help yourself...whether that be testing ideas or using the world as a mirror to try and improve yourself for the better.

there really is no downside. you will be criticized and you will be judged. the same happened to every human worth a shit throughout history...I think you'll be okay. 

2/4

on the flipside, Plutarch views withdrawing into obscurity as self-defeating and cowardly on all fronts. 

hence the medical analogy he uses...progress depends on shared experience, as we look for symptoms and cures for the "diseases of the soul."

whether you are good or bad is completely irrelevant. if you are like every other human that has ever lived, some of you is good, and some of you is bad. let future generations sort that out. humanity will find a use for whatever you've got going on.

but in "Living Unknown," you are depriving everyone. depriving yourself from improving, and depriving the world of your example.

3/4

especially if you read and write a lot, you develop a strange sense of civic duty... where you feel that no matter how your life turns out, for good or for ill, you are obligated to document your experience and try to say something in a way that hasn't been said before.

or, at the same time, you can offer yourself up as a diseased carcass to be analyzed....Ben Franklin's "Either write something worth reading or do something worth writing."

and then, when u expire, u toss it all onto this flaming wretched heap we call humanity in hopes that you may advance the ball by even an inch.

you're basically a living organ donor, in a sense. don't take yourself too seriously. every one of us is just a microcosmic speck in this strange science experiment we've found ourselves in.

4/4

I'm hoping this helps change your worldview. worry less about what people think of you today and worry more about what they'll think of you 500 years from now. 

if you read a lot, you already know: posterity is the only audience that anyone great has ever focused on. 

so, what you do with this information is up to you. but I think in deciding to live life hidden, in the shadows, Plutarch is correct to be somewhat condemnatory...all you're doing is depriving yourself and your fellow man.

you have nothing to lose and everything to gain

do not Live Unknown, friend.

advice I wasn't given until my 30's, that someone REALLY should have given to me in my 20's:

"Always be interviewing." Always, always know your "fair value" in the market.

Take every intvw, get an offer in writing, then push for even higher comp and get that in writing.

Go back to your current firm and say "you're paying me X, I have an offer away for 2x but I'd rather stay with you."

They'll match the offer because if you leave, they have to search, hire, screen, train, etc...from a time and energy perspective, its always easier to just pay you more.

There is no loyalty in corporate America, especially in finance... this is something everyone learns the hard way, and the truth is that nothing is ever personal.

All you're asking is to be paid what you're worth. These types of negotiations are literally why HR depts exist.

Some of the guys I've known in L/S who made the most $, they're not the most talented.

They're expert negotiators who somehow mastered the politics of bouncing from firm to firm, pod to pod, securing guarantees and bonuses and getting progressively higher comp each time.

Others I know who are insanely talented mgrs or analysts, but are humble individuals... they're out of work.

Despite L/S being fairly meritocratic, it's no different than the rest of the world... "everything is sales," and pitching stocks < pitching yourself.

I was never very good at this, usually I was the dumbest guy in the room and skewed towards "be humble, loyal, quiet, and don't rock the boat." 

But that's wrong, I was wrong, it's not how the world works. Don't be like that.

There is a quip that I think comes from Schopenhauer -- merit and modesty have nothing in common except the initial letter.

That is how shit really works. Merit doesn't win out...if there's a guy with less merit, but who wants it more, or who can sell the fuck out of himself, he will win. 

I have no angle here - this is a skillset I wish I had cultivated at a young age. 

If you have merit, wonderful -- having both [merit + sales] will take you much farther than merit alone. Make yourself into a dual threat, there is literally no reason not to...know what you're worth, ask politely to be paid what you're worth, and if I had to guess, you will be amazed how often you get it.

That's the advice I wish I was given in my early 20's. Good luck

most important lesson I learned in my 30’s is that you cannot manage other people’s perceptions of u.

I vividly remember being 34-35 and REALLY struggling with this so I'll explain.

(1/7)

people don't think, they feel.

in your mind u assume that everything about u is being weighed rationally and using the power of reason

in reality, there is no objective reality.

we live in stories. 

we have stories of ourselves and who we believe ourselves to be. 

the other people in our midst are comprised of stories that we have subjectively written about them. and you, in turn, are nothing but a story to others. there isn't just one "story" - each story is subjective and unique based on the individual author in question.

(2/7)

to some people, u are viewed thru a favorable lens, a favorable story. everything u say or do is filtered thru this lens.

their view of u is skewed (and incorrect) in that it's too rosy. their perception is too positive.

to others, u are viewed thru a negative lens, a negative story. ur words and actions are painted with this brush on arrival.

their perception is skewed and incorrect, just as the other person's was -- the only difference is the directional bias. one is too positive, one is too negative. 

in both cases, this is confirmation bias at work, and neither individual may even be aware of this information-filtering mechanism as it takes place.

(3/7)

what you need to understand, is that you are powerless to change either of these two perceptions.

"you cannot manage someone else's perception of you."

put another way, what other people think is none of your business.

humans are wildly irrational. if you haven't noticed, people perceive all sorts of slights or insults that were either unintentional, and quite often, never even occured. imaginations run wild and ppl dream up scenarios where someone is their best friend or worst enemy - with zero basis in fact.

(4/7)

you will drive yourself CRAZY trying to empathize "why does this person think what they do?"

because the truth, most of the time, is that they don't even know.

the subconscious is something like 95% of brain activity on the high end, or "the vast majority of it" on the low end. we have a very, very limited understanding of what makes us think, feel, say, and do the things that we do.

at some point, your actions, which are straightforward and logical to you, will be perceived on a wide spectrum by others. this will baffle you - how can all these people draw different conclusions about what I say or do, or even who I am as a human being?

(5/7)

but this is reality.

you are perceived differently, you have a different "story," in the mind of every single person you will ever meet.

is there room for their perception to shift positively or negatively based on your actions - of course.

yet how much power do u have to control their overall perception of you? very, very little...a number, for your own sanity, best rounded in your own head to zero.

(6/7)

the output is "stop caring what other people think." this is not meant in a sociopathic or thoughtless light. it means that u should do what u believe to be right, and recognize that ur "sphere of influence" extends no further than that.

you are powerless to shape how your words or actions are interpreted by the mind of a given recipient.

there is intention, and there is perception.

you can control your intention. you cannot control their perception.

so don't overthink it, and as a broad way of operating, don't bother trying to manage how other people perceive u... because u simply can't.

in the words of Buffett: “I have this complicated procedure I go through every morning, which is to look in the mirror and decide what I’m going to do. And I feel at that point, everybody’s had their say.”

(7/7)

paradoxically, what u will find is that u become a better person once u stop caring what other people think. 

it is very easy to bend over backwards trying to please other people, or at least doing what we perceive shall please them.

in this process, it is very easy to do the wrong thing while believing it to be right; because it wasn't done for you, it was done for the sake of other people.

yet in trying to manage other people's perception of u, u will not only drive yourself crazy, seeing as it doesn't work, but u will likely go astray, go against your own gut instinct, and effectively betray yourself.

by short-circuiting all of this -- simply doing what you know in your heart to be right, giving it no further thought, and controlling only what lays in your control -- u will find yourself achieving better outcomes with less stress.

that's why the lesson is so important.

as u watch people around u navigate life, over years and decades, u will see that attitude really does overpower everything

especially setbacks.

on one hand this is a frighteningly cliche observation; yet at the same time, like Munger's "show me the incentive and I'll show you the outcome," there are principles where the order of magnitude matters

i.e. you recognize it as a truth, but the all-pervading importance of it has to be further emphasized

on good vs bad attitudes...

GOOD: 

a person's attitude runs extremely deep. I don't think its something that can be altered.

this is one of those aspects of human nature, a mystery, where we'll land rockets upside-down on the sun before we understand how attitudes are hardwired

when you see someone with an exceptional attitude face adversity, its like an instinctual reaction: 

"nothing but a setback."

everything falls into that category. its all nothing but a setback. I'm always awestruck when I see it which is why this is my 500th tweet on attitude.

everything to them is an opportunity to improve, a test, a chance to prove themselves...everything is met with the question "what can I learn from this?" 

the belief that there are no losses, only lessons

u never see a person with a winning attitude complain...they accept constraints, and they find ways to win within them.

the book "The Diving Bell and the Butterfly" to me is the embodiment of an exceptional attitude, just the level of sheer willpower and determination required to make that happen.

BAD:

I won't dwell too much on bad attitudes because its pointless. a bad attitude can't be altered, nor does it have any interest in being altered. it was only in the last 3-6 months that I accepted this.

a bad attitude is the envious, victim mentality-type, always blaming and making excuses, always wallowing or attacking others.

a change in attitude would mean taking ownership of all one's flaws and shortcomings and failures. that means pain. its easier to keep blaming it all on the world.

once u see that someone is wired this way, just keep moving. u can go around trying to save people all u want -- u will eventually learn that some ppl have no interest in being saved.

THE PATH FORWARD

u have to take people as they come, one by one. 

they are unpredictable. rich, poor, where they grew up, what they do, where they went to school, none of that matters...there is zero correlation between attitude and anything else.

tweets.text:
"Familiarity Breeds Contempt."

very old proverb but one that u will find urself re-learning all across life

relationships, careers, friendship, love

it's an unpleasant concept but has to be internalized esp for work

(1/4)

photo below is from a bio on Roosevelt:

"Roosevelt accepted such compliments graciously, while being careful to avoid the familiarity which would assuredly breed contempt."

then goes on to explain this in practice

it's not just politics though, this applies for everything work-related -- has some ties to "is it better to be loved or feared."

this concept is unpleasant to me because it basically requires affectation thru any lens of work/politics

effective bosses or leaders u worked for, who seemed cold, or distant, or "asshole" to you... are just people who understood this hard truth of life:

"familiarity breeds contempt."

(2/4)

as u get older and have more and more ppl under you, or investors, or any blurring of the line between friendship and business, u have to be mindful of those three words.

also file under "Setting Boundaries."

I don't have the answer as to how this is best done, I struggle with it, I'm just bringing it to ur attention in hopes of helping u think differently.

at the most basic level though, this happens in many business relationships where u become friends too quickly -- and u recognize that they're afraid to give u direct feedback. mistake I've made a lot. u have to just bucket them as "friend," end the business side, find a replacement, and do a better job setting boundaries

(3/4)

in friendship this concept tends to be pretty straightforward

the things we find amusing at first, or that we put up with...end up being things we can't stand about our friends.

but friendship at its core is based on tolerating one another's faults - I'd argue that it's the only definition

a true friend will put up with your endless bullshit and set aside any contempt they have for your defects of character.

(4/4)

in love...this is where "familiarity breeds contempt" reigns supreme.

at the surface level, with someone u just met, too much familiarity too fast drives them away...it destroys whatever intrigue was there, shows that there's no mystery or depth to you...expressed as "he came on too strong," u moved too fast, u revealed desperation or that u arent a challenge.

once u successfully get past that phase...every long-term relationship ends up being defined at some point by the ways in which "familiarity breeds contempt."

the things u tolerated at first, u end up HATING about one another. everyone has lived thru this at least once.

if there's no communication, these little things quietly build and form resentment...which grows and grows until it all reveals itself in a blow-out fight

those can sometimes be devastating/point of no return

there is no solution to this, other than "communicate," because familiarity WILL breed contempt.

this is why the best advice is along the lines of: dont ever take someone conditionally, thinking "if I change x y and z they'll be perfect."

those won't change. u can't change people.

make sure that the flaws they come with, are ones u can live with...because they only become more glaring as time goes on.

END>>

this post could be a lot longer but I think the point is clear...its an unpleasant topic, an unfortunate truth of human nature, and one that if not internalized, will cause u problems in all facets of life.

"avoid the familiarity which assuredly breeds contempt."

on getting good sleep; I'm convinced the only thing that matters is putting 4-5 miles on the wheels each day

all the other stuff ppl do, the "sleep hygiene" routines, pale in comparison

0 miles = bad sleep, always
5+ miles = best odds (nothing is guaranteed)

five thoughts:

1. "sleep is more important than diet and exercise combined" - think this is factual/not even up for debate

key is u have to be maniacal about it throughout the day, at least while getting new habits in place

from the moment u wake up "what can I do to make sure I sleep good tonight"

once u get used to getting 8 hrs...and then u get 4, and u see how fucked up u are...u recognize that u are literally impaired. it happens, u just adjust for it - "not a good day for me to operate heavy machinery"

2. on walking 5+ miles...it sounds like a lot but once u aggressively break ur day down and look for any chunk of free time - its doable

it takes 2-3 months to put a new habit in place...they say 66 days or something comically accurate, but I agree, 60-90 days of daily discipline/dedicated focus and u can change ur lifestyle

best way to get there is in 2 blocks
-wake up early, train, move around
-early afternoon + sunshine
-if u can do more then do it...more movement >> better sleep. that 7-9 AM block where the sun is out is the holy grail bc ur body clock adjusts, but life/work tend to get in the way. someday...

3. jamming it into ur day

-take every possible phone call "on the hop"...say "let me call u back in 2 min," put on sneakers, go outside.
-stuff like replying to emails which u can do from ur phone, save for later in the day, then do it while walking around
-every possible "meeting," make it "lets just walk around," instead of lunch/drinks/coffee
-take the stairs everywhere
-if u have to be somewhere at 2 PM, and are free at noon, dont sit around doing nothing til 130 and take an uber...start walking there at noon even if its 20 miles away, knock out 5, then get a car when the timing lines up

4. perception

no one will think u are weird for this kind of shit

or, put another way, the ppl who will think u are weird...are the ppl who its okay to be thought weird by.

obsessive/psycho/high-performing mf's are all on this type of time

read bios of many great thinkers or authors and u see most of them walked insane amounts each day (8-10+ miles)

a lot of ppl who are "in shape," end up that way as an accidental output...they move around a lot to settle their mind and to get good sleep.

training is "for sanity, not vanity." everything is performance-driven, results-driven, output-driven...all these little steps and habits are incremental, they compound.

u have to be freakish and maniacal about this stuff, "put yourself first," dont worry abt perception...esp bc most people's response will be "damn thats actually a good idea."

5. on all the other stuff ppl do

theres nothing wrong w all the sleep masks, noise machines etc, but beyond that, the more natural the better

"there is no consequence-free drug"
"what goes up must come down"

everything u put in ur body that isnt natural will either leave u groggy, or refresh u at 90% and not 100%...all the supplements are nonsense, and all booze/drugs/pills come at a cost, esp caffeine which has a 5-6 hr half-life (ie stop drinking it 10-12 hrs before bed)

END>>

ultimately sleep is frustrating, its a unicorn...sometimes it just doesn’t come. all u can do is put urself in position to succeed.

but thats why I wrote this up...ppl do everything, except the most important thing...MOVE AROUND.

how to never get the morning blues - a step by step guide

1. 430 am alarm

2. STAND UP. walk to coffee maker, hit "on."

3. put on gym clothes, brush teeth.

4. fuel - 4-5 spoons of greek yogurt with honey/almonds/bloobs/banana + pound 2 cups of coffee the same way Roosevelt had his: "strong enough to float a horseshoe."

*get everything ready the night before; clothes, coffee, yogurt, etc

**ur supposed to brush ur teeth before u eat btw. I was 35 when I learned this

6. 445 AM: go time.

walk to wherever u train... airpods, deep house at max volume (partial to Kolter - "Be Real" this wk), try not to shit ur pants

shadowbox, be a freak, give thanks to the Most High that ur healthy and able to train...many men want nothing more than what u have in this moment

reflect on how many people squander the gift of health...scribble down notes "write a post about morning blues, maybe itll help someone"

7. pray for ur family and pray for ur friends. leave ur enemies to God

8. 100 weighted burpees

if ur out of shape do 10x5 with no weight. if ur in shape, knock off sets of 10, 5 singles 5 doubles

guy on the right is boxer Mike Rashid, we're trying to get to his level. copy his form, I had to put myself in the mix bc otherwise u get the gerbil squad... "rashid is big so hes on gear, not natty, fake video" etc....the pale white 40-yr old finance guy DQ's ur excuses.

9. after 2-3 sets I promise whatever "morning blues" u thought u had will be gone...rando free-floating anxiety is nowhere to be found and ur left only with "shit I have to do today/this week" i.e. actual worries

if ur pouring sweat, gasping for air and crouching to catch ur breath, ur doing them right

10. 530-545 pack it up, eat, shower, start ur day...commute, kids, narcoterrorism, whatever u do in the AM

11. soon as u start work do the most painful/unpleasant task immediately. this is old advice but it works

12. once this all becomes habitual u can be "done" with most of ur day by 9-10. only thing left is to walk a few miles in the sun and u will sleep good and live forever.

13. go to bed 830-9
14. 430 alarm
15. STAND UP + press "COFFEE" button. this is really 99% of the battle, u aint getting back in bed after that.

after that, 3 day rotation, push, pull, legs. honestly, if day 2 is just "do 100 various pull-ups" and day 3 is "do 100 various squats," and u just keep running this 3-day cycle for 3-6 months, u will pack on a lot of muscle

God gave u all the equipment u need, those few exercises cover almost ur entire body, and u dont have to think about shit at 430 am except "did I do legs yesterday"

END: NO DAYS OFF

Do not take days off, it is much easier to wake up early and train 7 days a week than 3-4. 

When u sleep in, u fuck up ur body clock, ur jet lagged all day, u sleep poorly that night, and then u will snooze the alarm.

Guess what comes after that... 

"The Morning Blues"

in this case u deserve them. sometimes the blues are simply God's way of telling u need to do better.

to borrow a Theodore Roosevelt term, the Blues are what u get for "living a life of slothful ease."

If TR was knocking motherfuckers out in bar fights at age 23 and then forcing them to "disdainfully" facechug beers afterwards, I'm pretty sure u can get up at 5 AM and do some pushups.

Best way to dodge the morning blues...don't ever let the sun catch u sleeping.

God bless ☀️

on why biographies are the best/most important books to read:

"...the book which has been most cherished and revered for well-nigh two thousand years is biography."

"Phillips Brooks once told the boys at Exeter that in reading biography three men meet one another in close intimacy—the subject of the biography, the author, and the reader."

these excerpts are so good - they're from the intro to Boswell's "Life of Samuel Johnson," written by an English professor at Princeton (Osgood)

three more

1. "Biography is the literature of realized personality, of life as it has been lived, of actual achievements or shortcomings, of success or failure; it is not imaginary and embellished, not what might be or might have been, not reduced to prescribed or artificial forms, but it is the unvarnished story of that which was delightful, disappointing, possible, or impossible, in a life spent in this world."

2. "In this sense it is peculiarly the literature of truth and authenticity. Elements of imagination and speculation must enter into all other forms of literature, and as purely creative forms they may rank superior to biography; but in each case it will be found that their authenticity, their right to our attention and credence, ultimately rests upon the biographical element which is basic in them, that is, upon what they have derived by observation and experience from a human life seriously lived. Biography contains this element in its purity. For this reason it is more authentic than other kinds of literature, and more relevant."

3. this 3rd paragraph is spectacular: "The thing that most concerns me, the individual, whether I will or no, is the management of myself in this world. The fundamental and essential conditions of life are the same in any age, however the adventitious circumstances may change. The beginning and the end are the same, the average length the same, the problems and the prize the same. How, then, have others managed, both those who failed and those who succeeded, or those, in far greatest number, who did both? Let me know their ambitions, their odds, their handicaps, obstacles, weaknesses, and struggles, how they finally fared, and what they had to say about it. Let me know a great variety of such instances that I may mark their disagreements, but more especially their agreement about it. How did they play the game? How did they fight the fight that I am to fight, and how in any case did they lose or win? To these questions biography gives the direct answer."

very important step for one's development as an investor or trader, that I wish I'd begun much sooner:

process vs outcome: documenting all events/catalysts by hit rate + taking a data-driven approach to everything you do.

(1/3)

biggest mistake ppl make, is not rubbing their nose in their own mistakes, or asking: "was I right for the wrong reason?"

I bring this up bc in the thread below, there's all sorts of binary setups listed...like "investor day" trades, or "lockup expiry" trades...all event-driven.

many of these are coin-flips, or 50-50 bets -- those are really your worst odds in markets. it's going up or it's going down.

but if you get a bunch of coin flips "right," and assume, wow, I have a natural knack for these, you're making an error in judgment.

(2/3)

La Rochefoucauld wrote that "self-love is more cunning than the most cunning man in the world" -- that's what you're trying to combat here. your mind will convince you that you're smart, when in reality, "good outcome" + "bad process" = WRONG.

so for something like a lockup expiry trade, if you've gotten say 10 out of 15 right, you have to ask: luck or skill? am I good at broadly analyzing these setups or are they stock-specific reads?

biggest Q always has to be = "what was my actual P&L?" meaning realized P&L... you have to evaluate the entire life-cycle of the trade...execution from start to finish. "I got the initial stock move right" doesn't equal "right," if on day 3 the trade realized red P&L.

(3/3)

this kind of brutal self-efficacy separates good from great... most ppl don't want to spend a Sunday afternoon staring at all their losses.

but without this ongoing self-evaluation, sorting everything by process vs. outcome, batting/slugging avg, you're not really making progress.

the path to determining what you do well, your "circle of competence," is mostly defined by years...if not decades... of steadily X'ing out all the things you DON'T do well.

one tricky thing about navigating life that I’d pass onto someone younger, is that you will get the best advice from people one-on-one behind closed doors

both the good and bad outcomes of whatever paths you’re considering

the phrase I’ve used that seems to resonate with people is that “everything in life has trade-offs”

what happens otherwise is that you follow this sort of broad “society” voice which is generally people who are programmed…just repeating what they were told “do this, do that” but if you ask them - WHY do you believe what you do? - you’d get a blank stare in return

the risk here is that you blindly follow a path that either runs against your instinct, or where you just have no inclination at all…because what happens is when you get there, and you then turn to society and ask, “what now?”

they’ll snap back at you - “why the fuck are you asking me?? I have my own problems, my own bills to pay” etc

and it’s very easy to feel like you got played, in some sense…you blindly followed a path to nowhere. That shit will make you feel like a coward.

quotedTweet.text:
fwiw -- that chart is illuminating if you've ever tried to short accelerating revenue growth/SSS%.

biz can be structurally unprofitable...unit economics don't work at any level of revenue

mkt wont bite.

this is super important to understand esp if you're new to L/S and short-selling in general

you will never get paid on EBITDA/EPS while revs are beating and raising, save for rare "bought the comp" / GM% implosions

this sounds like a simple lesson but I have probably lost more money shorting dogshit businesses with accelerating revenue growth than anything else.

because it wasn't clear to me that this rule is damn near ironclad. if a stock is "revenue today, profits manana," your model for that stock should have one line item

revenue

thats it. throw the rest of the fuckin model in the trash...the real wise man waits for them to miss #'s and then shorts it down 25% bc he knows its going down 80%.

most ppl shorting stocks dont grasp this, they jump in the way of momentum over and over. took me FOREVER to stop doing that shit - risk mgmt matters more than any individual short position.

be patient, if its as bad a business as u think it is, ur better off with a lower cost basis + lower risk, vs higher basis but fighting rev accel/momentum

example: $100 with upside mo vs. $80 with downside mo -- you want the $80 every time.

this doesn't become intuitive until you've been shorting stocks for many years and suffered immense brain damage.

also have heard it said that if its going to zero, whether u short it at $80 or $40 is irrelevant -- $ position size is the same and 100% max gain is the same.

if you subscribe to that point of view, you may as well wait for the 2nd miss as confirmation that the story is totally broken, then short it down 50%...some wisdom there, the 1st miss you still got the "true believers."

TL;DR - treat that rev growth as an ironclad rule and never assume u will get paid until it rolls.

remember that the tape shapes the news and not vice versa

few thoughts:

1/5

past few months reminded me of this tweet below + the tape at that time (3/31/2025)

before "liberation day" the nasdaq traded like a bag of ass every single day for ~2 months...bleeding lower.

hence why ppl who have been trading mkts for a long time got that eerie feeling - "we could crash."

that's captured in the tweet below, the notion of, it's not about the catalyst. the catalyst could be anything.

2/5

markets don't crash from all-time highs. its when you have a "sick" tape with weak leadership, just sort of floundering -- like we've had recently -- where the mkt is vulnerable.

dont look for news to backfit px action - just respect px action. ppl don't do this -- hence "omg a 2028 substack bear case crashed the market"...my man, it definitely did not lol...do not insult the market's intelligence like that.

but that gets us where we are now...the headline "war in iran," 3-6 months ago, a strong tape shrugs that off + rotates $ into unaffected sectors. 

the impact of "liberation day" type events, is not discrete - it's shaped by the underlying health of the tape.

3-6 months ago was a rotation tape. now... based strictly on px action, when you see things like "the nikkei just sold off 7% in a straight line," you may be in a correction tape.

3/5

no need to try and shoehorn news around it. the mkt tends to sniff out peaks in EPS growth, it tops out and turns lower.

doesn't mean the cycle ends - could sell off, base for 6 months, and let stocks get cheaper while waiting for new leadership to emerge + liquidity/stimulus from all angles + handoff from secular to cyclical growth.

but don't sit here expecting that we're down on a headline and will go up on the next headline. read the tape...its unhealthy, don't ask why, don't search for reasons why, just respect it.

4/5

"stop doing what isn't working."

watch the 52w highs list - 203 names with $2B+ in mkt cap printed yday...it's just not the 203 that everyone owns. 

you can buy software -50% ytd or buy petrobras +50% ytd. what twtr is doing isn't important - look at the tape and you'll see what "they" are doing. basic mats/energy/industrials are roaring.

the indices could get bashed around a bit, but real downturns never happen with cyclical growth is going apeshit to the upside.

5/5

so -- "DON'T READ NEWS, READ TAPE." 

there is no news, there never is, news will just put you on the wrong side of the trade. 

internals + movement under the hood, are your best guide as to what happens next...

mind ur risk + good luck trading.
